clue.text: Nonsensical language mostly used by sailors

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, so sailors gives ABS

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter, keeping most of it

parts.note: Urdu is a language of Pakistan and India

explanation.surface: A complaint that the jargon spoken by seamen makes no sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter; ABs are able seamen, a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absurd is ridiculous or illogical, a plain synonym for nonsensical.

clue.text: Maxim of a government department adopted by solid type

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: adopted by means the department is taken inside the solid, held within it

parts.note: a prism is a solid figure in geometry
HO is the Home Office, a UK government department

explanation.surface: A saying about a ministry being taken up by some kind of firm type of person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'type' is only a link word; the Home Office is the British interior ministry.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphorism is a short pithy saying, a close synonym of maxim.

clue.text: Hack riles BBC reporter initially

indicators.note: to hack is to chop up roughly, so the letters that follow are cut about into a new order
initially means only the opening letter of reporter is used

explanation.surface: A tabloid writer annoys the national broadcaster's correspondent from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' does double duty: it signals chopping up RILES and BBC into SCRIBBLE, and the whole clue describes such a writer. No other anagram signal is present.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribbler is a dismissive term for a poor or prolific writer, just like a journalistic hack.

clue.text: Bird scoring Charlie off criminal

indicators.note: scoring off, like crossing out, means that letter is struck from the word
off completes the phrase scoring off, signalling the letter is removed

parts.note: a crook is a criminal
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A bird ticking off a criminal, as if keeping score.
explanation.definitionFit: The rook is a black crow-family bird common in Britain.

clue.text: Mixed mood aboard Nordic conveyance

indicators.note: aboard means the mood is carried inside the vehicle

parts.note: a sled is a snow vehicle, apt for Nordic lands
a huff is a sulky mood

explanation.surface: Mixed feelings aboard a Scandinavian sleigh.
explanation.definitionFit: Shuffled cards are mixed, so the past tense of shuffle fits mixed.

clue.text: Shove over to accommodate journalist bearing a warning

indicators.note: to accommodate means the reversed shove takes the rest in its middle
over means the word for shove is turned round in this down entry

parts.note: to push is to shove

indicators.note: bearing means the journalist carries the a within him, so it sits inside

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Telling someone to move along to make room for a reporter who brings a caution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses the shove word; 'bearing a warning' looks like one phrase but 'bearing a' is wordplay and only 'warning' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A heads-up is an informal advance notice or alert, so it serves as a warning.

clue.text: Female murderer is clutching earl's trinkets

parts.note: Jack the Ripper was a notorious murderer, and a ripper is such a killer

indicators.note: clutching means the letters of is grip the earl's letter inside them

parts.note: E is an abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: A woman killer grabs a nobleman's ornaments.
explanation.definitionFit: Fripperies are showy trifles or cheap ornaments, the same idea as trinkets.

clue.text: Discovered alien language

indicators.note: discovered is read as dis-covered, its covers removed, so the outer letters go

parts.note: a Klingon is an alien race from Star Trek

explanation.surface: Someone has found out about an extraterrestrial tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' strips the first and last letters, K and N, from KLINGON.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal for a language or jargon, especially a foreign one.

clue.text: Native Americans supporting extremely divisive statute

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means the Native Americans come below
extremely means only the extreme letters of divisive, first and last

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people of Canada

explanation.surface: Indigenous people backing a highly controversial law.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree is an official order with force of law, akin to a statute.

clue.text: Dumb revolutionary is allowed outside Norway

indicators.note: revolutionary means the word is gets turned round
outside means allowed goes around Norway's letter

parts.note: let means allowed
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: A stupid rebel has been given permission to go beyond Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dumb' looks like an insult for the revolutionary but means unable to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumb in its older sense means mute or speechless, which is silent.

clue.text: Damage rare coin with tip of archaeological instrument

parts.note: to harm is to damage

indicators.note: rare as in underdone or unusual suggests the letters of coin are set out unusually
tip of means just the first letter of archaeological

explanation.surface: Spoiling an unusual coin by scraping it with the point of a dig tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rare' turns COIN into ONIC; 'instrument' poses as the archaeologist's tool but is the musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica is a mouth organ, a musical instrument.

clue.text: Olympic organisation welcomes reintroduction of popular Greek dialect

indicators.note: welcomes means the organisation takes the reversed word inside

parts.note: IOC is the International Olympic Committee

indicators.note: reintroduction is read as re-introduction, bringing in the word backwards

parts.note: in means popular, as in the in thing

explanation.surface: The Olympic body embraces the return of a well-loved ancient Greek tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reintroduction' is read as re-introduction: the popular word comes in backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic was the dialect of ancient Greek spoken in Ionia, used by Homer and Herodotus.

clue.text: Polish boy's rear is red

parts.note: to rub is to polish

indicators.note: rear means only the last letter of boy's is used

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about shining a lad's bottom until it glows red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with its capital pretends to be the nationality but is the verb to buff.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby names a deep red colour, after the gemstone.

clue.text: Decadent peers call underworld figure

indicators.note: decadent means decayed or degenerate, so the letters of peers fall into disorder

parts.note: to phone is to call

explanation.surface: Dissolute aristocrats ring up a gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld figure' suggests a criminal boss; it is the Greek queen of Hades.
explanation.definitionFit: Persephone is the goddess who rules the Greek underworld beside Hades for part of each year.

clue.text: No country includes Puerto Rico in accolade

indicators.note: includes means the country holds the Puerto Rico letters inside

parts.note: Belize is a country in Central America
PR is the postal abbreviation for Puerto Rico

explanation.surface: A geography note: no Central American nation contains Puerto Rico, said in praise.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nobel Prize is among the highest honours, an award or accolade.

clue.text: Betrayed only uncertainty in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the phrase is spoken, and it then sounds like the answer

parts.note: only means sole and uncertainty means doubt, so sole doubt

explanation.surface: A betrayed person whose only feeling, when talking, is doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell out is to betray one's principles or allies, so sold out means betrayed.

clue.text: Romeo enters stage delivering line of dialogue

indicators.note: enters means Romeo goes into the word for stage

parts.note: a phase is a stage
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo walks on stage and speaks his line in the play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romeo' and 'stage' paint a theatre, but Romeo is just R and stage is PHASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase is a short group of words, such as a single spoken line.

clue.text: Shopkeeper mixes 20 with it

indicators.note: mixes means the letters of the combined words are stirred together

parts.note: the answer to 20 Down is treason

explanation.surface: A trader who blends another entry with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer keeps a shop selling paper, pens and other writing materials.

clue.text: Strangely heartless, collecting debts in despicable manner

indicators.note: collecting means the shortened word gathers the debts inside it
heartless means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: oddly means strangely
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted debt collector behaving oddly and contemptibly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the central letter, leaving ODLY; IOUs are written promises to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means hateful or repugnant, so acting odiously is behaving contemptibly.

clue.text: Love musical about island in East Asia

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: about means the musical wraps round the island letter

parts.note: Rent is a Broadway musical

explanation.surface: Adoring a stage show set on an island somewhere in the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient is an old term for the countries of the East, especially East Asia.

clue.text: Model given cause for offence

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car
a reason is a cause

explanation.surface: A fashion model given a reason to take offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the crime of betraying one's country, a grave offence.

clue.text: Reactionary spotted object beside a road behind hospital

indicators.note: behind means a road comes after the hospital letter

parts.note: a die is a cube marked with spots

explanation.surface: A conservative spotted something by a road at the back of a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' looks like seen, but describes the dotted die.
explanation.definitionFit: A diehard resists change stubbornly, as an extreme conservative or reactionary does.

clue.text: Spirit of protest consuming a nationalist

indicators.note: consuming means the protest swallows the a inside it

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: The spirit of a demonstration taken over by a patriot.
explanation.definitionFit: A daemon is a supernatural being or guiding spirit in Greek myth.

clue.text: A bishop ships article out to monks

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop

indicators.note: out means the article is removed from the ships

parts.note: boats are ships
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A bishop sends an item abroad to the brothers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like an item shipped but is A, the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbots are the heads of abbeys of monks, so monks of senior rank.

clue.text: He swears sheep lamb around middle of April

indicators.note: around means the letters are turned about into a new order
middle of means the central letter of April

explanation.surface: Sheep and lambs in the fields in mid-spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals rearranging SHEEP and LAMB into BLASPHEME; 'He swears' looks like a person vowing but means one who curses.
explanation.definitionFit: A blasphemer speaks irreverently of sacred things, so he is one who swears or curses.

clue.text: Stone portal south of Anatolian capital

indicators.note: in a down entry, south of means the portal sits below
capital means the capital, or first, letter of Anatolian

parts.note: a gate is a portal

explanation.surface: A stone gateway south of a Turkish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anatolian capital' suggests Ankara but gives only the letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded semi-precious stone, a form of chalcedony.

clue.text: Drunk overcome by remorse, essentially

parts.note: to win is to overcome

indicators.note: essentially means the essence, the central letter, of remorse

explanation.surface: Someone drunk and overwhelmed with regret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' poses as a description of the remorseful person but is the noun; 'overcome' is WIN, and O is the middle letter of REMORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wino is an alcoholic, especially one living rough, so a drunk.

clue.text: Satirical piece set in Hell's Kitchen

indicators.note: set in means the answer lies within the letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: A comic sketch set in the New York district of Hell's Kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch, often parodying something.

clue.text: A gumshoe tailing fair creature

indicators.note: tailing means a gumshoe follows behind the word for fair

parts.note: OK means fair or acceptable
a gumshoe is a private detective, a PI

explanation.surface: A private eye shadows a fair-skinned creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailing' fits a detective following someone; here it just orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is an African animal related to the giraffe.

clue.text: Raiments of monarch seized by retreating highlanders

indicators.note: seized by means the monarch is held inside the reversed word
retreating means the highlanders word goes backwards

parts.note: Scots live in the Highlands
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A king's robes captured by highland clansmen as they fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' gives STOCS; 'Raiments' is an old word for clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockings are leg garments, so items of clothing, raiments in an old word.

clue.text: Female workers touring northern drinking establishments

parts.note: she is a female pronoun

indicators.note: touring means the workers go around the northern letter

parts.note: worker bees, so bees are workers

explanation.surface: Women employees on a pub crawl round the north.
explanation.walkthrough: A shebeen is an unlicensed drinking den, a term from Ireland and South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Shebeens are illicit bars or drinking dens, so drinking establishments.

clue.text: Reliable research sustains professor's conclusion

indicators.note: sustains means the research holds up the letter within it

parts.note: study is research

indicators.note: conclusion means the last letter of professor's

explanation.surface: Dependable research backs up an academic's findings.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdy means robust and dependable, hence reliable.
